{{*}} [[Gnome glider]] |music = *[[Anywhere]] * [[Monkey Madness (music track)|Monkey Madness]] * [[Island Life]] |map = {{Map|name=Ape Atoll|zoom=1|x=2750|y=2750}} |type = island |leagueRegion = Kandarin }} {{Relativelocation|location=Ape Atoll|east=Kharidian Desert|north=Karamja|west=Feldip Hills}} '''Ape Atoll''' is an island in the [[Ardent Ocean]] of [[Gielinor]], home to a vibrant population of [[monkey]]s. The settlement of [[Marim]], where the monkeys reside, is under the rule of [[Awowogei|King Awowogei]]. It is only accessible to players who have partially or fully completed the [[Monkey Madness I]] quest. Players who have not taken the form of a monkey using a [[greegree]] will find themselves the target of [[aggressive]] creatures throughout the island. Being spotted by the monkey locals or interacting with them may result in the player being knocked out and sent to the prison in Marim. However, upon completion of [[Monkey Madness II]], a greegree becomes unnecessary for this purpose as all surface inhabitants become tolerant towards the player. [[Monkey zombie]]s and [[Skeleton (Ape Atoll)|skeletal apes]] remain aggressive to those without a greegree, however. The island is teeming with dangers including [[Monkey Archer|Ninja Monkey Archers]] and [[Monkey Guard (ninja)|Ninja Monkey Guards]], [[Monkey Guard|Gorilla Monkey Guards]], poison-inducing [[Snake (Ape Atoll)|jungle snakes]] and [[Jungle spider (Ape Atoll)|spiders]], and environmental hazards such as a collapsing cave. As a result, Ape Atoll is widely regarded as one of the most hazardous regions in ''[[Old School RuneScape]]'', particularly for those new to the challenges it presents. ==Transportation== Initial access to Ape Atoll requires the player to first travel via [[Lumdo]] on [[Crash Island]] during [[Monkey Madness I]]. To get there, speak to [[Daero]]While it was previously impossible to return to Ape Atoll after completion of [[Monkey Madness I]] without receiving experience from [[Monkey Madness I#Rewards|Daero's Training]], an [[Update:The Garden of Death & More#Poll 77 Changes|update in November of 2022]] now allows the training to be ignored before returning. on the {{FloorNumber|uk=1}} of the [[Grand Tree]]. From there, have [[Waydar]] fly you to Crash Island. There are several alternative transportation methods available after completion of [[Monkey Madness I]]: *A [[Fairy ring]] ({{Fairycode|CLR}}) will take players to the [[Ape Atoll Agility Course]]. 48 [[Agility]] and a [[ninja monkey greegree]]Without a [[ninja monkey greegree]], jumping over the river with the [[Rope (Ape Atoll Agility Course)|rope]] will cause the player to fail the obstacle, take some damage and return to the start of the agility course. This will put players in jail if [[Monkey Madness II]] is not completed. are required to exit the course and travel to the city. One can exit the course by failing the rope obstacle in human form (however this still requires level 48 Agility to attempt the obstacle). *The level 64 [[Ape Atoll Teleport (standard)|Ape Atoll Teleport]] is available in the [[normal spellbook]] after [[Recipe for Disaster/Freeing King Awowogei|Freeing King Awowogei during Recipe for Disaster]]. The spell takes the player to the safe upstairs section of the [[Temple of Marimbo]] in the north-east corner of Ape Atoll. *The level 90 [[Ape Atoll Teleport (Arceuus)|Ape Atoll Teleport]] in the [[Arceuus spellbook]], as well as the equivalent [[Ape atoll teleport (tablet)|magic tablet]], takes players to the [[Ape Atoll Dungeon]] on the southern part of the island. *The [[Gnome glider|Gnome glider network]] can take players to the north-west of the island after completion of [[Monkey Madness II]] by choosing the Ookookolly Undri destination. The fastest way to access the glider network is by climbing to the top floor of the [[Grand Tree]]. {{Reflist}} ==Island features== [[File:Marim.png|thumb|The centre of Marim, featuring a statue of [[Marimbo]].]] ===Marim=== {{main|Marim}} The marketplace in Marim is home to several [[shop]]s and [[Stall#Thievable stalls|thievable stalls]]: {| class="wikitable" ! colspan=2 |Shop ! colspan=2 |Stall |- | {{plinkt|Solihib's Food Stall|pic=Food shop icon}} | {{plinkt|Food stall|pic=Banana}} |- | {{plinkt|Hamab's Crafting Emporium|pic=Crafting shop icon}} | {{plinkt|Crafting stall|pic=Chisel}} |- | {{plinkt|Ifaba's General Store|pic=General store icon}} | {{plinkt|General stall|pic=Pot}} |- | {{plinkt|Tutab's Magical Market|pic=Magic shop icon}} | {{plinkt|Magic stall|pic=Air rune}} |- | {{plinkt|Daga's Scimitar Smithy|pic=Scimitar shop icon}} | {{plinkt|Scimitar stall|pic=Iron scimitar}} |- | {{plinkt|Oobapohk's Javelin Store|pic=Archery shop icon}}Oobapohk's Javelin Store is only accessible to players who have completed [[Monkey Madness II]]. |} {{Reflist}} Notable among these is Daga's Scimitar Smithy, being the sole shop that sells [[Dragon scimitar]]s. Furthermore, completion of [[Monkey Madness II]] grants access to [[Ape Atoll bank]]. ====Temple of Marimbo==== {{main|Temple of Marimbo}} Situated at the eastern edge of the city lies the [[Temple of Marimbo]], which is home to several [[Monkey Guard]]s. The temple is a popular low-intensity training area, as there is a prayer altar inside. Players can use the [[Protect from Melee]] prayer to avoid damage and automatically fight the Monkey Guards until their prayer runs out, as long as [[Auto Retaliate]] is turned on and [[Monkey Madness II]] is not completed. The [[Temple of Marimbo Dungeon]] contains a large quantity of [[Monkey Zombie]]s and is an effective location for [[Ranged]] training. ===Agility course=== The [[Ape Atoll Agility Course]] located south of Marim is available at level 48 [[Agility]]. At lower Agility levels, the failure rate on obstacles makes efficient training unfeasible. You will need a [[Ninja monkey greegree]] or [[Kruk monkey greegree]] in order to make use of the course. After completion of [[Monkey Madness II]], players can obtain a [[Monkey (Monkey Madness II)|Monkey]] which they can equip on their back. The monkey can be transformed into six other variants by completing laps at the agility course. Note that laps will only begin to be tracked upon completion of Monkey Madness II; [[Bobawu]] can tell players how many laps they've completed. ===Ape Atoll Dungeon=== [[File:Ape Atoll Dungeon.png|thumb|The twisting pathways of the Ape Atoll Dungeon.]] The [[Ape Atoll Dungeon]] is a winding maze that has many dangerous areas. They include traps that can hit up to 8, [[Spider (Ape Atoll)|spider]]s that [[poison]] starting at 1, and undead monsters capable of hitting over 20. The [[aggressive]] [[Skeleton (Ape Atoll)|skeletal apes]] found here come in large quantities and provide high experience rates if killed with [[Multicombat area#Multi-hitting attacks|Multi-hitting attacks]], such as [[chinchompa (weapon)|chinchompas]] and [[burst spells|burst]]/[[barrage spells]]. ===Hardwood trees=== Ape Atoll features a decent supply of hardwood trees. At [[Cape Atoll]] in south-west corner of the island stand two [[Mahogany tree]]s, each slightly spaced from the other. Additionally, near the destination of the [[Ape Atoll Teleport (Arceuus)|Ape Atoll Teleport spell]] within the [[Arceuus spellbook]], three [[Teak tree]]s grow in close proximity to each other. These trees can be cut with a Greegree in hand, so that players can safely chop them down in a manner that ensures that the nearby monsters remain passive. ===Fishing spots=== There are two [[Fishing spot (big net, harpoon)|spots]] for [[Big fishing net|Big net]] and [[Harpoon]] [[Fishing]] situated on Ape Atoll. One is positioned to the east of the agility course, while the other is found at [[Cape Atoll]] on the south-western corner of the island. They can be fished for [[raw mackerel]], [[raw cod]], [[raw bass]], [[big bass]], [[raw shark]] and [[big shark]]. There are also non-fish items such as [[casket]], [[leather boots]], [[leather gloves]], [[oyster]] and [[seaweed]]. ===Kruk's Dungeon=== West of Marim lies the entrance to [[Kruk's Dungeon]], accessible both during and after the events of [[Monkey Madness II]]. A [[light source]] is needed to traverse its underground levels. Similar to the Ape Atoll Dungeon, this labyrinth provides an excellent arena for training using Multi-hitting attacks, with its [[Maniacal monkey]] inhabitants offering the potential for even greater experience rates. Furthermore, at level 60 [[Hunter]], players can capture certain [[Maniacal monkey (Hunter)|Maniacal monkeys]] by setting a [[Deadfall|Deadfall trap]]. This is referenced when charting the [[dictionary]] on [[Shimmering Atoll]]. *The name Ape Atoll is a reference to the Monkey Island point and click adventure games. *Ape Atoll is considered to be a difficult area to make changes and adjustments to in content updates, as it was primarily designed by intern [[Rahul Vohra]] in the summer of 2004. Vohra's background was in object-oriented programming, and his code is less intuitive and more difficult for Jagex's developers to work with than Jagex's own scripting system designed for non-programmers.https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=4837&v=PiBigfDrA4k *Ape Atoll has the shape of an ape's head looking east, including inlets for the eye and nostril. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Ape Atoll}} {{Monkey Madness I}} {{Monkey Madness II}} {{Regions}}
